title: Asparagus, canned, cooked with butter or margarine

content.title: About
content.content: Canned asparagus cooked with butter or margarine is a ready‑to‑eat vegetable product. The asparagus retains most of its nutrients, while the added fat gives a smooth flavor and aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Asparagus belongs to the lily family and is one of the oldest cultivated vegetables.
Canning allows asparagus to be stored for several years without loss of taste.
Cooking with butter enhances the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as vitamin K.
Asparagus is rich in antioxidants, including glutathione and vitamin C.
In the United States, canned asparagus is often served as a side dish with meat.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Asparagus provides folate (B9), vitamin B6 and niacin, which support metabolism and nervous‑system health.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: It contains potassium, iron and magnesium, important for muscle and heart function.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Dietary fiber promotes regular bowel movements and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Flavonoids and carotenoids protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Anti‑inflammatory properties
items.content: Bioactive compounds such as saponins may reduce inflammation in the body.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned products often contain added salt; people monitoring sodium intake should account for this.

items.title: Butter allergy or intolerance
items.content: Individuals with dairy‑fat sensitivity should choose a version prepared with margarine.

items.title: BPA in packaging
items.content: Metal cans can leach trace amounts of BPA; look for BPA‑free labeling if this is a concern.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned asparagus can be eaten cold in salads, warmed in the microwave or skillet, added to pasta, omelets or soups. For extra flavor, drizzle with lemon juice, sprinkle garlic or fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened can in a cool, dry place. After opening, transfer the contents to an airtight container and keep refrigerated for up to 3‑4 days. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
